svg.title: Transactional outbox
svg.desc: Commit the event with the data in one transaction; a relay publishes it later. The relay is drawn as a poller; log-tailing CDC (e.g. Debezium) plays the same role. Consumers are not drawn. Delivery is at-least-once: a relay crash between publish and mark-sent republishes the event, so consumers must deduplicate by event id. The backlog counter jumps to 3 at the start of the outage phase, and to 1 at the start of the publish phase, because the tool can only ramp counters on return legs. 1. Atomic write: order and event commit together. 2. Relay publishes: relay publishes it, then marks it sent. 3. Broker down: orders still commit; events wait. 4. Broker back: relay retries and drains the outbox.
